page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the Epdsv6 family. It is powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor running at 3.4 GHz, featuring 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 3780 GB of local storage and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with uncached large-block read and write speeds reaching top-tier levels. Single-core performance, however, remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests, highlighting a performance profile that favors highly parallelized workloads over single-threaded execution.

Given its high memory capacity, substantial local storage, and strong multi-threaded capabilities, the E64pds_v6 is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, and high-throughput web serving. Passmark database operations and static web serving benchmarks both rank in the top tier. The ARM-based architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency, making it a cost-effective alternative to traditional x86 architectures for parallel processing, software compilation, and large-scale database deployments.
